mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.2% over the next month, investors anticipate tighter policy, causing a short-term discounting effect that lowers expected equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger period (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS change is < 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in PAYEMS (labor market activity) accompanied by UNRATE falling below 4% suggests a tight labor market, which typically precedes equity risk-on flows and drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 5% in a month AND UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the trigger, or UNRATE does not fall below 4% when PAYEMS spikes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in HOUST (residential construction) above 2% for two consecutive months signals robust demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as optimism about future growth boosts equity prices.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month + 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the two-month building surge.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 3% predicts supply-side weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as market anticipates slower economic growth.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by > 3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative or flat during the contraction, or INDPRO recovers within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for a month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to turn negative due to market anticipation of rate hikes and reduced equity risk appetite.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or unchanged despite CPIAUCSL > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE to below 3% triggers a risk-on equity response as investors interpret lower unemployment as a sign of economic strength, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the UNRATE drop.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in GDPC1 (GDP) and PAYEMS (employment) by at least 2% in a quarter signal robust demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns as investors price in stronger economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by > 2% AND PAYEMS increases by > 2% over the quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the dual proxy increase.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged monthly decline in RSAFS (federal surplus) of 4% or more indicates fiscal tightening, which is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as market fears tighter financing conditions.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by > 4% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative during the fiscal tightening, or RSAFS recovers before the horizon.
